facts.claim: Stasiun Klimatologi Kelas II Bali (BMKG Climatology Station, Bali), at Jl. Lely No. 9, Negara, Jembrana, is the BMKG technical unit that handles climate and air quality information for Bali Province. It publishes 10-day rainfall forecasts, a monthly bulletin (rainfall analysis and 3-month outlook) and a season bulletin (forecast onset of the rainy or dry season).

Stasiun Klimatologi Bali, Buletin Iklim Bali, May 2024 edition (definitions page): 'Normal monthly rainfall' is the average rainfall for each month over a 30-year period; 'average monthly rainfall' uses a minimum 10-year period. Bali's monthly analysis and forecasts use rain-gauge posts across 20 season zones (Zona Musim, ZOM), the zoning set in 2021. A ZOM is an area whose average rainfall pattern shows a clear difference between the dry-season period and the rainy-season period; areas without that clear difference are 'non-ZOM'.

Stasiun Klimatologi Bali, Buletin Iklim Bali, May 2024 (definitions): season onset is stated in dasarian (10-day periods: days 1 to 10, 11 to 20, 21 to month end). The bulletin's worked examples read: 'rainy season onset around November I to November II = 1 to 20 November' and 'dry season onset around June I to June III = 1 to 30 June'. These are given as examples of the notation, not as a Bali forecast.

Stasiun Klimatologi Bali, Buletin Iklim Bali, May 2024 (definitions): daily rain intensity categories are very light under 5 mm in 24 hours, light 5 to 20 mm, moderate 20 to 50 mm, heavy 50 to 100 mm, very heavy over 100 mm.

Stasiun Klimatologi Bali, Buletin Iklim Bali, May 2024 (forecast for 2024 only, Bali Province): June 2024 rainfall generally 0 to 100 mm, July 2024 generally 0 to 150 mm, August 2024 generally 0 to 100 mm, with rainfall character generally Below Normal for all three months. This is a single-year forecast, not a long-term normal.

Stasiun Klimatologi Bali, Buletin Iklim Bali, May 2024 (analysis of April 2024 only): the highest monthly rainfall in Bali in April 2024 was 592.2 mm with 20 rain days in southern Buleleng (Sukasada district); the most rain days was 24 in southern Karangasem (Selat district); the highest one-day total was 160.0 mm in Klungkung district. Rainfall character for April 2024 was generally Above Normal. Single-month observations, not normals.

Stasiun Klimatologi Bali home page, news item 'Ringkasan Informasi Iklim Bulan Agustus 2026': analysed rainfall across Bali Province for July 2026 was 0 to 425.5 mm for the month (single-month observation; the full item was not read).

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: weather can change quickly during the wet season (usually around October to April; it can differ in Eastern Indonesia). Heavy rains can cause significant flooding in urban areas including Bali, disrupting roads and transport. No temperature or rainfall figures are given.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: volcanic activity may escalate with little or no notice, causing flight delays, cancellations or airport closures, including in surrounding provinces; Mount Agung in Bali Province is listed among volcanoes to watch, and trekking routes on or near Mount Agung and Mount Batur are named. Indonesia uses a 4-level volcano alert system (Normal, Advisory, Watch, Warning). Contact your airline for the latest flight information.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: Indonesia is in an active earthquake region with a high level of earthquake activity that sometimes triggers tsunamis; high wave events can happen in coastal regions. Know the emergency plans at your accommodation. Australians have drowned in rough seas and rip currents at popular beaches including in Bali.

[Copied from bali-wedding-venues 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Smartraveller Indonesia: rabies is throughout Indonesia and 100% fatal once symptoms develop; get vaccinated before travel, avoid contact with dogs, cats, monkeys and bats, and get urgent care if bitten or scratched; rabies treatment may be limited. Dengue occurs including in Bali, and periodic measles outbreaks are reported including in Bali.

insider_details.detail: BMKG times season onset in 10-day blocks (dasarian) and by season zone, and Bali has 20 zones, so onset can differ between, say, Jembrana and Karangasem. Ask the Wedded Advisor to check the zone for your venue, not just 'Bali'.

Even in a month BMKG rates wet, totals vary hugely across the island (April 2024: up to 592.2 mm in Sukasada, with a 160 mm single day in Klungkung). Plan a covered or indoor wet-weather option whatever month you choose.
Staklim Bali publishes a 3-month rainfall outlook every month; check the latest bulletin about 90 days out to sense-check your date and rain plan.

Nyepi falls on Monday 8 March 2027, right before the Idul Fitri holidays and collective leave (9 to 15 March), so avoid that fortnight for a wedding weekend and book flights early if guests travel then.

Smartraveller puts Bali's wet season at around October to April with fast-changing weather and urban flooding, so a wet-season date needs a covered or indoor ceremony back-up and generous transfer buffers.

Glass and clifftop chapels (AYANA Tresna, Mulia, Apurva Kempinski Kimaya, St. Regis Cloud Nine) keep the ocean view under cover, but published seating is small, so confirm capacity before treating one as the rain plan.
Volcanic ash can close airports with little notice, so build a spare day before the wedding into guest travel advice.
